messages.text: What are the most important signal generation capabilities for applications in Wireless Communication?

The most important signal generation capabilities for Wireless Communication applications are:

1. **Wide RF frequency coverage**  
   A generator should cover the key wireless bands. For example, the R&S®SMBV100B covers **8 kHz to 6 GHz**, described as covering “all important RF bands for digital wireless communications.”  

2. **Wide RF modulation bandwidth**  
   Modern 4G, 5G, Wi‑Fi 7 and future wireless standards need large bandwidths. The SMBV100B supports up to **1 GHz RF modulation bandwidth**, which is cited as meeting demanding 4G and 5G requirements.

3. **Excellent signal quality**  
   Wireless receiver, transmitter, and conformance tests depend on clean reference signals. The cited SMBV100B material highlights **excellent signal quality** as a core performance characteristic.

4. **High output power**  
   High output power is important for test setups with path loss, OTA chambers, cables, fixtures, or DUTs requiring strong input levels. The SMBV100B is specifically described as combining **high output power** with wide bandwidth and signal quality.

5. **Support for very wide wireless waveforms**  
   For Wi‑Fi 7 and beyond, the ability to generate or verify very wide signals is critical. R&S cites verification of a **480 MHz bandwidth** Wi‑Fi 7 waveform in loopback mode with the CMP180.

6. **Multi-standard capability**  
   Wireless labs often need one setup for cellular and non-cellular technologies. R&S cites a one-box tester setup that can test **cellular and non-cellular latest-generation standards**, including Wi‑Fi 7.

7. **OTA test integration**  
   For modern wireless devices, especially 5G and Wi‑Fi, signal generation must work in OTA environments. The CMX500 and SMBV100B are cited as integrated with **ETS-Lindgren chamber technology and EMQuest™ software** for comprehensive wireless testing.

**Raw evidence used:**  
- R&S®SMBV100B specs: high output power, wide modulation bandwidth, excellent signal quality, 8 kHz–6 GHz range, up to 1 GHz RF modulation bandwidth.  
- R&S Wi‑Fi 7 PR: CMX500/CMP180 support for Wi‑Fi 7, cellular/non-cellular testing, and 480 MHz waveform verification.  
- R&S / ETS-Lindgren PR: CMX500 and SMBV100B integration with OTA chamber technology and EMQuest software.

passages.text:
The R&S®SMBV100B vector signal generator combines superior performance characteristics such as high output power, wide
modulation bandwidth and excellent signal quality. With a frequency range from 8 kHz to 6 GHz, the instrument covers all important
RF bands for digital wireless communications. The wide RF modulation bandwidth of up to 1 GHz satisfies the challenging
requirements of fourth and fifth generation communications standards. In A&D applications, the wide bandwidth allows the generation
of complex pulsed signals.

Rohde & Schwarz will display its [R&S CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester at MWC 2024 with newly added Wi-Fi 7 testing capabilities. With this functionality, the one-box tester allows R&D engineers of wireless devices to comprehensively test their design’s operation in cellular and non-cellular standards of the latest generation in a single instrument setup. In addition to this, the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester will verify a signal waveform of 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, attesting to be a future-proof solution for users in R&D and production, even beyond the requirements of Wi-Fi 7.

answer.text:
Wide RF frequency coverage: the R&S®SMBV100B covers 8 kHz to 6 GHz, which “covers all important RF bands for digital wireless communications.” [5]
Wide modulation bandwidth: up to 1 GHz RF modulation bandwidth, satisfying demanding 4G and 5G communications requirements [5].
High output power and excellent signal quality, both identified as core performance characteristics of the vector signal generator [5].
Support for very wide wireless waveforms, such as verification of a 480 MHz bandwidth signal waveform for Wi‑Fi 7 and beyond [6].
Integration with OTA chamber technology and test software, since the SMBV100B is integrated with ETS-Lindgren chamber technology and EMQuest software to support comprehensive wireless testing [1].
Multi-standard wireless test capability, including cellular and non-cellular latest-generation standards in a single setup, as shown by Wi‑Fi 7 capability alongside cellular testing [6].
